title: Taller Is Not the Same
story: The class tested whether identical seedlings grew better in full sun or in light shade. They planted two trays of the same lettuce in the same compost and gave each tray the same water every morning. One tray sat on the open bench. The other sat under a cloth that let light through but softened the midday heat. Every Monday they measured the height and wrote it in a shared table. After three weeks the shaded plants were taller, but their stems were thin and they leaned. The sunny plants were shorter and sturdier, with deeper colour in the leaves. Amina said that taller did not always mean healthier. The class then counted how many plants stayed upright after a windy night, and more of the sunny ones did. Their conclusion stayed careful. Shade had changed the shape of the growth, and one measurement would have told only part of the story.

vocabulary.definition: Very young plants grown from seed.
A rich soil mix used for growing plants.
Stronger and less likely to bend or break.
An area protected from full sun.

quiz.question: What did the class keep the same for both trays?
options: The lettuce, the soil mix, and the water each morning
The cloth, the shade, and the midday heat
The windy night and the leaf colour
The height of every stem after three weeks
quiz.correctAnswer: The lettuce, the soil mix, and the water each morning
quiz.explanation: Both trays had the same lettuce, the same compost, and the same water every morning.
quiz.supportingSentence: They planted two trays of the same lettuce in the same compost and gave each tray the same water every morning.

quiz.question: How did the shaded plants look after three weeks?
options: They were taller, but thin and leaning
They were shorter and harder to bend
They had the same height and colour as day one
They had all fallen before any measuring
quiz.correctAnswer: They were taller, but thin and leaning
quiz.explanation: After three weeks the shaded plants were taller, but their stems were thin and they leaned.
quiz.supportingSentence: After three weeks the shaded plants were taller, but their stems were thin and they leaned.

quiz.question: What point was Amina making about the tall plants?
options: Extra height did not by itself prove they were healthier
The sunny plants had failed because they were short
Height should be the only number in the table
Lettuce grows well only under a cloth
quiz.correctAnswer: Extra height did not by itself prove they were healthier
quiz.explanation: Amina said that taller did not always mean healthier.
quiz.supportingSentence: Amina said that taller did not always mean healthier.

quiz.question: Why would one height check have been a weak conclusion?
options: It would have shown only part of how the plants changed
It would have given one tray more water than the other
It would have proved that shade has no effect
It would have made both trays the same colour
quiz.correctAnswer: It would have shown only part of how the plants changed
quiz.explanation: Shade changed the shape of the growth, and one measurement would have told only part of the story.
quiz.supportingSentence: Shade had changed the shape of the growth, and one measurement would have told only part of the story.

quiz.question: What does sturdier mean in this story?
options: Stronger and less likely to bend
Taller, with a thin stem
Hidden under a garden cloth
Written as a number in a table
quiz.correctAnswer: Stronger and less likely to bend
quiz.explanation: The sunny plants were shorter and sturdier, unlike the thin leaning ones, so they were stronger.
quiz.supportingSentence: The sunny plants were shorter and sturdier, with deeper colour in the leaves.
